title: "dicer kernel import"
description: "Import a kernel to boot instances with"
---

Imports a kernel that instances can boot. FILE is a kernel on this
machine, of up to 512 MiB. It is sent to the daemon, and the command
returns once the kernel is on the daemon's host. If `--sha256` is given, the
kernel is checked against it. An instance that names no kernel boots the
default kernel, which needs no import.

## Usage

```console
$ dicer kernel import NAME FILE [flags]
```

## Examples

```console
$ dicer kernel import k6 ./vmlinux --arch x86_64
```

## Flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--arch string` | Kernel architecture, e.g. x86_64 (required). |
| `--sha256 string` | Expected SHA-256 of the kernel, hex-encoded. |

## Global flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-D`, `--debug` | Trace every call to the daemon on stderr (or set `$DICER_DEBUG`). |
| `-r`, `--remote string` | Daemon to talk to: a remote's name, or an address (unix:///PATH or HOST:PORT) (default `$DICER_REMOTE`, then the current remote, then local). |
| `--request-timeout duration` | Give up on a single call to the daemon after this long, e.g. 30s (0: never; streams such as logs -f and exec are not bounded). |
